about: The contract of the ClaxBot surfaces host protocol (docs/contract.md, "ClaxBot surfaces"), as examples both sides replay.

`messages`: every message, each as the type named reads and writes it. `tolerated`: what a reader takes that is not written so: what a daemon may send that a host built on this version still reads, and what a host may leave out. `refused`: what the side that reads a message refuses.

`script`: one life of two registrations of the surface in `files`, in order, by a clock that starts at 0 (`at_ms`). A step with `host` is a request and its answer; one with `run` is what a run's side does or sees: `call` (a script's call for a registration: the ID the daemon gives it, or the error the script is thrown), `outcome` (what the script is answered or thrown, at that instant), `waiting` (the call is not settled), `ended` (a run of the registration's ended). Its calls are made under a policy that sends nothing again (one attempt): a run on the daemon has three (docs/contract.md, "Sending a call again"), so where its host answers `unavailable` (at_ms 59) or is not connected (at_ms 40000) the daemon first sends the call again, or waits for the host, until the call's deadline.

Where the script has an ID of 32 zeros, it is one the daemon never gave. A string `$file:<name>` stands for the text of `files[<name>]`. A string `$<name>` is an ID the daemon chose: the same name is the same ID throughout, and different names are different IDs. `$_` is any value. `held_ms` on a serve is how long the daemon holds it before it answers.
